actual.letter:
I write as the registered keeper of vehicle KX19PLT in respect of Parking Charge Notice PCN778899. I dispute liability for this parking charge and require the operator to consider this appeal.

The Parking Charge Notice alleges: Overstayed the maximum permitted period at Riverside Retail Park.

Where the operator seeks to recover the parking charge from the registered keeper rather than the driver, it must establish that the statutory conditions for keeper liability under Schedule 4 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012 have been satisfied. Keeper liability does not arise merely because an individual is the registered keeper.

This appeal is submitted by the registered keeper. No admission is made as to the identity of the driver, and nothing contained within this appeal should be interpreted as identifying or inferring the identity of the driver.

The operator has not established the identity of the driver. As the applicable Schedule 4 requirements have also not been satisfied, liability cannot be transferred to the registered keeper under Schedule 4.

The Notice to Keeper does not contain a compliant route-specific keeper-liability warning. The operator cannot rely upon Schedule 4 where the applicable statutory conditions have not been met.

For the verified reasons set out above, the operator has not established keeper liability under Schedule 4 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012. The charge should therefore be cancelled as against the registered keeper.

On the operator's own documents the parking event took place on 12 June 2026, the Notice to Keeper was issued on 2 July 2026; the statutory period for delivery of the notice ended on 26 June 2026 and it is deemed delivered on 6 July 2026, 10 days outside that period, so the notice was not delivered within the statutory period and keeper liability does not transfer.

The Notice to Keeper was not delivered within the applicable statutory period for the relevant postal-notice route. The operator has therefore failed to satisfy a condition required to transfer liability to the registered keeper under Schedule 4.

The allegation that the applicable parking tariff was not paid is disputed. A payment was made in connection with the vehicle's use of the site. The operator should review its payment records against the parking event before continuing enforcement.

The operator is requested to conduct a reasonable search of its payment records for the relevant location and period, including transactions capable of being matched to the parking event rather than relying solely on an immediate VRM match.

The allegation turns on whether a required validation, authorisation or payment step was completed at the site. The materials available to the keeper do not establish that step one way or the other. The operator is requested to review its validation, kiosk, permit and transaction records for the vehicle, location and material date, and to explain the specific records relied upon before maintaining the charge.

For the reasons set out above, the parking charge is disputed and the operator is requested to cancel the Parking Charge Notice.
